name: Marine collagen / hair vitamins
lead: Marine collagen and "hair vitamin" products are oral dietary supplements marketed for hair thickness, shedding and general hair health. Formulations vary widely and commonly combine collagen peptides, often sourced from fish, with vitamins, minerals and botanical extracts.

Published evidence for these multi-ingredient products is limited in the sources reviewed here. Several small, mostly single-product trials of hair supplements have been registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, including studies in people with hair thinning and shedding [1][2][4][9], but this article does not report outcomes for them because results were not available in the sources used.
infobox: Collagen peptides, vitamins, minerals, botanicals (varies by product)
Sold as supplements; formulations differ by brand

paras: Hair vitamins are sold as capsules, gummies or powders. Marine collagen versions use collagen peptides derived from fish skin or scales. Because there is no standard formula, "hair vitamin" describes a product category rather than a single compound.

Registered trials of hair-focused nutraceuticals include a 100-person study of a dietary supplement for hair thinning and shedding [1], a 25-person single-group study of a hair vitamin combination [2], a 110-person study of a supplement with vegan botanicals in women with self-perceived thinning hair [4], and further studies of nutraceuticals in female pattern hair loss and telogen effluvium [8][9][10]. A planned trial will examine a supplement for telogen effluvium associated with GLP-1 receptor agonist use [3]. Each tests a specific commercial formulation, so results for one product do not necessarily apply to another. No outcome data are summarised here.

Supplement stacks for hair are listed among the oral products that people use alongside topical and prescription hair-loss treatments. No community sources were available to document specific claims in detail.

quick.overview:
Marine collagen and hair vitamins are oral supplements sold to support hair thickness and reduce shedding. They are a broad category, usually combining collagen peptides with vitamins, minerals and plant extracts.

Several small trials of specific products have been registered, but published outcome evidence was not available in the sources reviewed.
quick.mechanism: Makers generally propose that supplying collagen-derived peptides and micronutrients supports the hair follicle and hair shaft. The sources reviewed do not establish a mechanism.
quick.risks: Safety depends on each product's ingredients. No safety data were available in the sources reviewed; supplements are not regulated like prescription drugs.
